title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection with varying local densities is hard for distance-based methods, which miss local anomalies, and density-based methods, which need parameter tuning and incur quadratic time. SVEAD addresses this by building an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams via uniform anchor sampling and scoring each point by its normalized distance to its anchor weighted by the cell mean distance, then averaging scores across partitions. On 45 ADBench datasets, SVEAD (printed as VEAD in the tables) reports the highest average AUC-ROC of 0.8538 and AUC-PR of 0.5000, and on the target cardio dataset it reports AUC-ROC 0.9339.

match_target.why: User's target hint is Table 4, SVEAD AUC-ROC on cardio; C1 is exactly that single-dataset result. It is the cheapest quantitative check that still exercises the full SVEAD pipeline (anchor sampling, Voronoi assignment, dual-factor scoring, ensemble averaging) and the paper's central claim that SVEAD detects anomalies without density parameters.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports std 0.0063 for SVEAD/VEAD AUC-ROC on cardio over 5 runs (Table 5, cardio, last column); 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189, rounded up to the 4-decimal precision printed in Tables 4-5.

requirements.stmt: Sample m anchors uniformly without replacement from the full dataset for each of t partitions.
requirements.quote: For each partition, we randomly sample m points from the dataset X without replacement to form an anchor set

requirements.stmt: Assign every point to its nearest anchor using Euclidean distance, forming Voronoi cells.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈X is assigned to its nearest anchor, creating a partition {C1, C2, . . . , Cm}

requirements.stmt: Compute per-cell δmax and δmean from all points assigned to the cell.
requirements.quote: computing cell statistics including maximum and mean distances

requirements.stmt: Score each point by s(x) = (δ/δmax) · δmean within its assigned cell.
requirements.quote: where the first term δ/δmax normalizes the distance by the maximum cell radius, and the second term δmean represents the mean distance within the cell.

requirements.stmt: Skip scoring a point in a partition if its cell contains only the anchor.
requirements.quote: In the rare case where a cell contains only the anchor (|Ci| = 1), we skip scoring for this point in this partition

requirements.stmt: Average the per-partition scores over the ensemble to obtain f(x).
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean

requirements.stmt: Use ensemble size t=100 for SVEAD's reported tables and grid-search m over {2^1,...,2^8}.
requirements.quote: For Isolation Forest, iNNE, IDK, and SVEAD, the number of sample points is searched over

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 5 times and report the average AUC-ROC and AUC-PR.
requirements.quote: For each dataset and method, we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance.

requirements.stmt: Use labels only after unsupervised scoring to compute AUC-ROC and AUC-PR.
requirements.quote: the labels are used to compute the AUC-ROC and AUC-PR for each dataset only after the models have made predictions.

requirements.stmt: Run baselines from PyOD except SLAD and DTE from official repositories when reproducing Table 4.
requirements.quote: Most algorithms are implemented from the PyOD library (Zhao et al., 2019), while SLAD and DTE are obtained from their official repositories.

requirements.stmt: Preserve linear time complexity O(nmdt); avoid full Voronoi diagram construction.
requirements.quote: The total time complexity is O(nmdt) + O(nmdt) = O(nmdt)

requirements.stmt: Do not require k-NN or distance-threshold parameters; use geometric proximity only.
requirements.quote: Voronoi cells are defined purely by geometric proximity without requiring neighborhood size or distance threshold parameters.

data.name: Synthetic datasets S1 (global), S2 (local), S3 (dependency)
data.how_to_get: Generate as described in Appendix A: 300 samples each, 10% anomaly rate; S1 Gaussian normal + uniform peripheral anomalies, S2 two moon-shaped dense clusters + between-cluster anomalies, S3 positive linear dependency normal + negative-correlation anomalies.
